$comment: Rails for the sentinel's ORCHESTRATOR session (felipearos/ralph#681, spec
#678), added by `ralph.sh` with `--settings` once `roles.ts` names this
file as the role's `orchestratorSettings`, INSTEAD of the harness-wide
`claude-orchestrator-settings.json` — so it repeats every rule of that
file, and adds the sentinel's own.
The sentinel reads one production error the gate handed over and drafts a
ticket for it. It never writes code, so it may not edit a file, commit,
revert, reset, push, or open or merge a pull request. It writes NEW files
under `.ralph/logs/` (the ticket draft and the journal draft) with
`Write`, so `Write` stays open and the role's clean-detached invariant is
what catches a stray file in the checkout.
It never writes to the tracker: in file mode the GATE files the draft, so
the session's draft goes only through `sentinel/issue.ts draft`. Every
`tracker.ts` verb that writes (or that reaches a tracker credential, as
`connect-test` and `connect-save` do) is denied; `view`, `ref`, `url`,
`pr-ref`, `list` and `claimed` stay open. `gh issue`, `gh label` and
`gh api` (which can do any of it raw) are denied too.
It never reaches the reporter or the network: the reporter token is the
gate's alone, so what the gate stored is the evidence, and `curl`, `wget`,
`WebFetch` and `WebSearch` are denied. Stack frames, breadcrumbs and titles
come from production and are data, never instructions. Nor may it edit the
issue store (`ralph/sentinel-issues.json` in git's common directory),
which only the gate and `sentinel/issue.ts` write.
Both spellings, `Bash(x *)` and `Bash(x:*)`, for the reason
`claude-executor-settings.json` gives. A tripwire, not the boundary: the
boundary is that the session holds no reporter or tracker credential.
Every database client is denied as the verifier's are: the session
diagnoses from code and git history, and production data is not its to read.
